## Question 2: [Title that matches the question, e.g. "Do critics and audiences agree?"]

### Introduction

[Question, variables (rotten_tomatoes, metacritic, cinema_score, release_date), why you are interested.]

### Approach

[Two different plot types and why each one is the best choice. At least one uses color or facets.]

### Analysis

```{r}
#| label: q2-data
grades <- c("A+" = 100, "A" = 97, "A-" = 93, "B+" = 90, "B" = 87, "B-" = 84,
            "C+" = 80, "C" = 77, "C-" = 74, "D+" = 70, "D" = 67, "D-" = 64, "F" = 57)

q2 <- game_films_raw |>
  mutate(audience = unname(grades[cinema_score]),
         critic   = (rotten_tomatoes + metacritic) / 2,
         gap      = audience - critic) |>
  filter(!is.na(gap))
```

```{r}
#| label: q2-gap-over-time
#| fig-cap: "Audience minus critic score over time"
ggplot(q2, aes(release_date, gap)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(color = "#08519c", size = 2.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Release date", y = "Audience minus critics (points)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#| label: q2-biggest-gaps
#| fig-cap: "Films where audiences and critics disagreed most"
q2 |>
  slice_max(abs(gap), n = 8) |>
  ggplot(aes(reorder(title, gap), gap, fill = gap > 0)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Audience minus critics (points)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

[What the plots show, why, and limitations (small sample, fans may inflate CinemaScore, letter grades converted to numbers).]
